scope: Contextless finished-prose read of the three supplied files only. No source audit, runtime inspection, network access, edits to inputs, or publication.

findings.quote: This revision records complete per-execution captures and requires the external supervisor in both prepared CPU and target commands.
findings.finding: The unqualified "This revision" reads as the current tpu,cpu preparation, although the report says per-execution capture checks and the supervisor were already present in ed17 and are unchanged. The preceding "first preparation" is similarly undated. A future reader cannot reliably place these corrections before the new ambient-backend change.
findings.suggested_wording: The earlier ed17 revision added complete per-execution captures and required the external supervisor in both prepared CPU and target commands. Those corrections and their controls are retained unchanged in this tpu,cpu preparation.
findings.note: Likewise label the "New-fixture development" paragraph as earlier fixture history if that is the intended chronology.

findings.quote: AST comparison proves every worker statement outside provenance is unchanged from ed17.
findings.finding: The preceding paragraph identifies both provenance changes and new fail-closed backend checks. "Outside provenance" leaves it unclear whether backend validation is included in that category, so the two delta descriptions appear inconsistent when read alone.
findings.suggested_wording: The source audit confirms that the changes are limited to provenance and backend validation; the fixture execution logic is unchanged from ed17.
findings.note: If preserving the AST-specific claim, name the exact audited block instead of "provenance"; this read did not inspect or validate the audit.

checks.title: The proposed title starts with the imperative "Prepare" and states the concrete change.
checks.boundaries: The texts distinguish CPU results and installed-source reasoning from actual TPU success, original-environment fidelity, and full-model acceptance. No wording issue found in those boundaries.
checks.device_identity: The matching default and explicit TPU device lists describe checks within a target execution; the prose does not claim identical physical chips across runs.
checks.ceremony: The release and authorization boundary is repeated, but no additional approval or process is requested by this read.
